div.head: II Cn 31.1a
div.ab: ⁊ gyf man þone hlaford teo, þæt he be his ræde ut hleope, ladige hine mid V þegnum ⁊ beo him sylf syxta.
And gyf man þonne hlaford teo, þæt he be his rede ut hleape, ladige hine mid fif þegnum ⁊ beo him sylf syxta.
Et si dominus accusetur, quod eius consilio fugerit, adlegiet se cum V táinis (id est nobilibus) et ipse sit sextus.
⁊ gyf hi ðone laford teon, þæt he be his rǽde ut leope, ladige hine mid fif ðegnum ⁊ beo him sylf syxta.
And gyf man þone hlaford teo, þæt he be his ræde ut hleope, ladige hine mid V þegnum, and beo him sylf syxta.
Und wenn der Herr beschuldigt wird, dass auf seinen Rath jener entflohen sei, reinige er sich mit fünf Thegnas und sei selbst Sechster [im Eide].
And if the lord is accused of the man having escaped on his advice, let him clear himself with five thegns and be himself the sixth [in the oath].
And if the lord is accused of advising him to escape, he shall clear himself with [the help of] five thegns, himself making a sixth.
And if the lord is then accused, that it was by his advice that he ran away, he is to clear himself with five thegns, and be himself the sixth.
And if the lord is accused of advising him to escape, he must exonerate himself with the support of five thanes, and himself will make the sixth.
